name: vscode-julia-format

scripts.all: pnpm check && pnpm build && pnpm package
scripts.upd: pnpm up --latest && pnpm dedupe && pnpm up -s

description: A formatter for the Julia language

julia-format.args.markdownDescription: Command line argument(s) for Julia. See [Command-line switches for Julia](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/manual/command-line-interface/#command-line-interface).

julia-format.flag.default: style=DefaultStyle(), indent=4, margin=256, always_for_in=true, for_in_replacement="∈", whitespace_typedefs=true, import_to_using=true, whitespace_in_kwargs=true, align_struct_field=true, align_assignment=true, align_conditional=true, align_pair_arrow=true, normalize_line_endings="unix", align_matrix=true, join_lines_based_on_source=true, indent_submodule=true, surround_whereop_typeparameters=false, yas_style_nesting=true

julia-format.inop.markdownDescription: The `in`-like operator(s) for doing `for_in_replacement`, seperated by space. Or, set this to empty string to use the default rule of `JuliaFormatter`. Note: This no longer works with [JuliaFormatter v2.9.0+](https://github.com/JuliaEditorSupport/JuliaFormatter.jl/commit/1f1f388f794add3495a308b5dbd2e3ae116db043#diff-c0cc23b54ebc2c42a6eeaa572df5204a030c72c9f1ee47073f2de1a00404c808L933-L934), and you have to set `always_for_in = nothing` instead.

julia-format.tabs.markdownDescription: Tab size, which should be the same as `indent`'s value in `#julia-format.flag#`. Or, set this to 0 to use space(s).
